pages.t: Aginet is not a separate company. It is the name TP-Link uses for its offer to internet providers. TP-Link's own service provider site lists Aginet Solutions alongside its router, mesh, PON and LTE product categories.
g: Internet Service Provider, the company that sells internet subscriptions to homes and businesses.

pages.t: TP-Link describes Aginet Solution as an end-to-end Wi-Fi management solution for ISPs. It is a mix: devices the provider hands to its customers, and cloud tools the provider uses to set up and look after them.
g: Covers the whole chain, from the box in the home to the tools the provider uses.

pages.t: Many people think Aginet means fibre boxes only. It does not. The line also covers routers, mesh units and 5G routers. On TP-Link's provider site, models like HX510 are Wi-Fi mesh units and NX510v is a 5G router, not fibre terminals.
g: Several Wi-Fi units that work together as one network in a home.

quiz.q: What is Aginet?
o: TP-Link's name for its offer to internet providers
quiz.w: Aginet is the brand TP-Link uses on its service provider site for devices and management tools aimed at ISPs.

quiz.q: Which description of Aginet Solution matches TP-Link's own wording?
o: An end-to-end Wi-Fi management solution for ISPs
quiz.w: TP-Link calls it an end-to-end Wi-Fi management solution for ISPs.

quiz.q: A colleague says Aginet is only fibre terminals. What is the best correction?
o: It also includes routers, mesh and 5G routers
quiz.w: The line includes several device types plus the management tools around them.

pages.h: The end customer is a provider
pages.t: Aginet is aimed at ISPs and service providers, including smaller wireless ISPs. They often give or rent a box to every subscriber, so they usually care about cost per home, support calls and easy rollout.
g: Wireless ISP, a provider that delivers internet over radio instead of cable or fibre.

pages.t: Equipment placed at the customer's home is called CPE. It can be bought by the subscriber or supplied by the provider. Aginet is aimed mainly at the second case: boxes the provider chooses and manages remotely.
g: Customer-premises equipment: router, gateway, set-top box or similar at the customer's site.

pages.t: Allnet is a distributor, so we sell to resellers and integrators who serve providers and network owners, not to households. The question to ask: who in the chain picks the box for the subscribers?
g: A company that buys from the vendor and sells to resellers, who sell to end customers.

quiz.q: Who makes the buying decision for an Aginet deployment?
o: The provider that supplies the box to its subscribers
quiz.w: Aginet is for providers who supply and manage devices for many subscribers.

quiz.q: What does CPE mean?
quiz.w: CPE is equipment at the customer's site, such as a router or gateway.

quiz.q: Which cost concern is most typical for a provider buying CPE?
o: Support calls and rollout effort per subscriber
quiz.w: Providers multiply every box by thousands of homes, so support and rollout effort matter a lot.

lessons.title: Fibre to the home and PON

pages.t: In a PON the fibre in the street is passive: no powered equipment in between. A splitter divides one fibre from the provider so it can serve many homes, which means fewer powered parts to run and maintain.
g: Passive Optical Network, fibre network shared by many homes through passive splitters.

pages.t: The OLT sits at the provider and sends the light out. The ONT sits at the customer and turns light into normal network ports. Think of the ONT as the fibre's front door.
g: Optical line terminal, the provider's end of a PON.
Optical network terminal, the single-customer box that receives the fibre.

pages.t: GPON is the long-standing mainstream generation. XGS-PON is the newer 10 gigabit symmetrical generation, meaning the same speed up and down. A seller only needs to know which one the customer's network uses.
g: Same speed for download and upload.

quiz.q: What makes a PON 'passive'?
o: No powered equipment in the fibre path between provider and home
quiz.w: Splitters in the field need no power, so there is no powered equipment between provider and home.

quiz.q: Which box sits in the customer's home and receives the fibre?
quiz.w: ONT is the customer-side terminal. OLT is the provider side.

quiz.q: A provider is moving to XGS-PON. What does that mainly tell you?
o: They are moving to a 10 gigabit symmetrical fibre generation
quiz.w: XGS-PON is the 10 gigabit symmetrical PON generation.

quiz.q: Why must a seller ask which PON type a customer uses?
o: Because it decides the colour of cables
Because the fibre device must match the provider's network generation
quiz.w: A fibre terminal must match the network it connects to, GPON or XGS-PON.

pages.t: Setup 1: a separate ONT plus a normal router behind it. Setup 2: one gateway with the fibre part and Wi-Fi built in. Setup 3: a small fibre module that plugs into a device with a matching socket.
g: One box that combines the line connection and the router.
A small pluggable module slot used for fibre connections.

pages.t: TP-Link announced an XGS-PON Wi-Fi 7 router and a plug-in XGS-PON module in October 2023. Routers such as EX520v and NX220v have an Ethernet WAN port, so they can sit behind an ONT or other modem.
g: The port that connects the router to the provider's network.

pages.t: Ask: does your fibre arrive in an ONT already, or do you want one box? If an ONT is in place, a router with an Ethernet WAN port may be all they need. If not, the integrated model matters.

quiz.q: A provider already puts an ONT in every home. What does the subscriber still need?
o: Only a router with an Ethernet WAN port
quiz.w: With an ONT in place, a router with an Ethernet WAN port can handle the home network.

quiz.q: What is an SFP module in this context?
o: A small pluggable fibre connection module
quiz.w: SFP modules plug into a matching socket and carry the fibre connection.

quiz.q: Which statement about Aginet is safest?
o: Every Aginet model has a fibre port built in
TP-Link has announced Aginet devices with XGS-PON built in, while others use Ethernet from an ONT
quiz.w: The range mixes announced XGS-PON devices with routers that connect to an ONT via an Ethernet WAN port.

pages.t: Wi-Fi 6 was designed for the 2.4 and 5 GHz bands. Wi-Fi 6E is Wi-Fi 6 that also uses the 6 GHz band. Wi-Fi 7 uses all three and adds wider channels and multi-link operation. Newer is not always needed.
g: A radio frequency range Wi-Fi uses. More bands give devices more room.

pages.t: EasyMesh is a Wi-Fi Alliance standard for several access points to act as one network. It also allows access points from different vendors to be added, so a provider can extend coverage later.

TP-Link's provider pages list HX510 and HX710 as Wi-Fi 6 mesh systems that are EasyMesh compatible. EX520v and NX220v also list EasyMesh, so units in one provider's range can work together. Check details per model.

quiz.q: What does Wi-Fi 6E add compared with Wi-Fi 6?
quiz.w: 6E extends Wi-Fi 6 with the 6 GHz band.

quiz.q: What is EasyMesh?
o: A Wi-Fi Alliance standard for access points working as one network
quiz.w: EasyMesh lets multiple access points form one unified Wi-Fi network.

quiz.q: A provider asks how its subscribers can get Wi-Fi coverage in larger homes. What fits?
o: Add EasyMesh access points such as HX510 where coverage is weak
quiz.w: EasyMesh units can be added to extend coverage where needed.

pages.t: TP-Link's provider site lists Wi-Fi routers, home Wi-Fi systems (mesh), VDSL, PON and LTE, with 4G/5G routers under LTE. Together they cover copper lines, fibre and mobile networks, so one vendor can serve a provider with mixed technologies.
g: Broadband over old copper phone lines.

pages.t: On TP-Link's provider site: EX520v is a Wi-Fi 6 router with a phone port, HX510 and HX710 are mesh units, and NX220v and NX510v are 5G routers with a voice port for a normal phone.
g: A port for a normal landline phone, used for voice over internet.

pages.t: Think in three steps. Fixed line: fibre or copper router. Mobile network: 5G router. Bigger home: add mesh units. Ask which access network the provider has first.
g: Fixed wireless access: home internet delivered over a mobile or radio network.

quiz.q: Which device suits a provider selling home internet over a 5G network?
quiz.w: NX models are 5G routers. HX are mesh units and EX520v is a fixed-line Wi-Fi 6 router.

quiz.q: What is HX510 mainly?
quiz.w: TP-Link describes HX510 as a Wi-Fi 6 whole-home mesh system with EasyMesh.

quiz.q: What is the first question when picking an Aginet device?
o: Which colour does the customer like
What access network the provider runs
quiz.w: The access network, fibre, copper or mobile, decides which family fits.

quiz.q: Why does a phone port matter to some providers?
o: It lets customers keep a normal phone over internet voice
quiz.w: Models like EX520v and the NX routers offer a voice port for a normal telephone.

pages.t: A provider cannot send a technician to every home. With a standard like TR-069, a server called an ACS can set up devices, check status, update firmware and run diagnostics remotely.
g: A long-standing standard that lets a provider's server manage devices at customer homes.
Auto-configuration server, the provider's management server.

pages.t: TP-Link names TAUC (the cloud platform), Aginet ACS, Aginet Config and Aginet App. TAUC is built on TR-369 and TR-069, and lists zero-touch deployment and troubleshooting tools.
g: A newer management standard, also called USP.
Devices set themselves up with no manual work.

pages.t: In a meeting: the provider can set up, update and troubleshoot customers' boxes from one place. Fewer visits and fewer support calls. Do not go into protocol detail unless the customer's technician asks.

quiz.q: What does an ACS do?
o: Manages customers' devices remotely from the provider side
quiz.w: An ACS is the provider's server that configures and monitors devices remotely.

quiz.q: Which is the best one-sentence benefit of TAUC for an ISP?
o: Boxes can be set up and troubleshot remotely, cutting visits
quiz.w: Remote setup and troubleshooting reduces technician visits and support effort.

quiz.q: A customer asks about TR-069 support. How do you respond at sales level?
o: Confirm it is part of how Aginet devices are remotely managed and offer a technical contact
quiz.w: Datasheets and TP-Link pages list TR-069 support, but deep protocol answers belong to a technical contact.

pages.t: Aginet Config lets a provider set its own default settings for all devices, including a logo and favicon. The settings come back when a customer presses reset, which can reduce repeat support calls.
g: The small icon shown in a browser tab.
Wiping a device back to its default settings.

pages.t: The Aginet App gives subscribers a way to manage their network and run diagnostics. TP-Link says it supports ISP co-branding, so the provider's brand is visible rather than TP-Link's alone.
g: Showing two brands together, here the provider's and TP-Link's.

pages.t: A provider wants the box to feel like its own service. Branding and a ready-made app can save them building these tools themselves. Ask how much customisation they need before promising specifics.
g: Selling a product under another company's brand.

quiz.q: What happens after a customer factory-resets a device with Aginet Config defaults?
o: It reverts to generic TP-Link defaults
It keeps the provider's configured defaults
quiz.w: TP-Link states the configured defaults persist after a factory reset.

quiz.q: What does the Aginet App let subscribers do?
o: Manage their network and run diagnostics
quiz.w: It is an end-user app for managing the network and running checks.

quiz.q: A provider asks for a fully custom app design. What is the safest answer?
o: TP-Link lists ISP co-branding, but check exact options with TP-Link before promising
quiz.w: Public sources only confirm co-branding, so exact scope must be checked.

lessons.title: Aginet versus retail TP-Link and others

pages.t: A retail router is set up by the buyer. An Aginet device is meant to be set up and managed by the provider. The hardware may look similar to what people know, but the tools around it are what the provider is buying.

Aginet pairs devices that look like everyday routers with a management platform built for providers. That platform is what TP-Link itself stresses, also for smaller providers. Whether it beats other makers is not something we can prove here.
Providers can also buy from other CPE makers or have boxes built to their own spec. We have no verified comparison, so do not claim you are better. Ask what they use today and what is missing.
g: Hardware made to one provider's own specification.

quiz.q: What is the main difference between a retail router and an Aginet device?
o: Aginet devices are meant to be managed by the provider
quiz.w: The provider management tools are the point of the Aginet line.

quiz.q: A customer says a rival CPE is better. What should you do?
o: Ask what they use today and which gaps they want to close
quiz.w: We have no verified comparison, so discovery questions are safer than claims.

quiz.q: What does TP-Link itself stress about Aginet?
o: A provider management platform around the devices
That it is the cheapest option
quiz.w: The provider-side management tools are the core of the Aginet offer.

pages.t: A local fibre network owner runs ONTs already and wants a home router plus remote support. Think router with Ethernet WAN, TR-069 and the Aginet tools, and add mesh units for big homes.

A provider has fibre in towns and 5G in rural areas. TP-Link's pages list routers, mesh and 5G models that all support TAUC cloud management, so one platform can cover them. Confirm the exact setup with a technical contact.
'It is a consumer brand': answer with the provider management tools. 'Do you have my exact feature': ask a technical contact. 'Is the newest Wi-Fi needed': only if their customers need it.

quiz.q: A fibre network owner already has ONTs. Which first suggestion fits?
o: A router with an Ethernet WAN port plus remote management
quiz.w: With ONTs in place, the home device can connect via Ethernet WAN and be managed remotely.

quiz.q: A provider has fibre in town and 5G in rural areas. What is the strongest point?
o: Fixed, mobile and mesh devices can sit under one management platform
quiz.w: TP-Link product pages list TAUC support across router, mesh and 5G models.

quiz.q: A customer says TP-Link is only a consumer brand. What is a good reply?
o: Point to the provider management tools in Aginet
Say consumer brands are always better
quiz.w: The provider-side tools are what separate Aginet from shelf products.

quiz.q: A customer asks about an exact feature you cannot verify. What do you do?
o: Say yes to win the deal
Check with a technical contact before answering
quiz.w: Never promise unverified features.
